key_insight: iCSNNs extend graph neural networks to stationary multivariate time series by using inverse cross-spectral density matrices as frequency-specific shift operators, capturing both temporal and cross-variable dependencies.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a compact, learnable way to model frequency-dependent interactions in multichannel signals, which is useful for forecasting, diagnosis, and structured representation learning.
method: Derive graph shift operators from inverse cross-spectral density (iCSD) matrices in the Fourier domain.
Group frequencies into bands that share one iCSD operator to exploit spectral smoothness and reduce parameters.
Jointly learn the dependence structure and iCSNN weights so the operators adapt to the downstream task.
evidence_signal: On synthetic data, iCSNN outperformed baseline methods from multiple methodological families.
watch_item: The approach assumes stationary multivariate time series and relies on accurate estimation of cross-spectral structure, which may be challenging with limited or noisy data.
paper_title: Inverse Cross-spectral Neural Networks for Multivariate Time Series
